add.issue.name: Settings panel: the gear does not close a panel the avatar opened; Escape in a dropdown closes the panel; an armed trash never disarms

edit.description.md:
Review of 4SC2RXY at 858da367 (`SettingsPanel.tsx`, `App.tsx`, `ReposSettings.tsx`). Each reproduced in the browser. All small; fine after merge.

**1. The gear does not close.** `toggleSettings` in App.tsx closes only when the panel is open at the gear's own focus (`overview`), so a panel opened from the avatar or the palette's Link repo stays open on the first gear click, while the gear is drawn pressed. Fix: the gear closes whenever the panel is open.

**2. Escape in a dropdown closes the panel.** The Dropdown's Menu and the panel both use `useDismissOnOutsideClick`, which listens on the document; one Escape fires both, so picking branches and backing out loses the panel. The URL field already stops propagation; the Menu should too, or the hook should honour `defaultPrevented`.

**3. The trash stays armed.** `useArmed` in ReposSettings has no blur or outside-click disarm (the claim button has `onBlur`), so a row stays washed red until another trash is pressed or the panel closes.

Nits: `fetchLinkedRepos` (e2e-gui/linked-repos.ts) sets `process.env.EPIQ_GLOBAL_DIR` for the rest of the worker; `IdentityPanel.tsx` now exports `IdentityAddresses`.

add.issue.name: Other repos: a linked repo with no commits yet reads as "its history could not be read" under the default branch

edit.description.md:
Full-feature review of 4SC2RXY at 858da367, `source/lib/commits/commit-sources.ts:97`. Reproduced through the real code (fetch, then `listRepoStates`).

A clone under `branches: default` is read with `git log HEAD`. On a remote with no commits yet HEAD is an unborn branch, and git answers `fatal: your current branch 'main' does not have any commits yet` (exit 128). The fetch itself reports ok and the timeline reads as empty, but `readSourceLogs` notes the failure, so the panel's row shows "its history could not be read" and an info line is logged per fetch. Under `branches: all` the read is `--branches`, which answers nothing and succeeds.

Fix: `--branches` for both settings (a default clone holds only the default branch: the refspec fetches one, and `dropOtherBranches` removes the rest after a switch), or `--branches=<name>` from the clone's HEAD. Add the empty-remote case to the reading tests.

Fine after merge.

add.issue.name: Settings panel: never takes focus nor hands it back; a label rename makes every client refetch its history

edit.description.md:
Full-feature review of 4SC2RXY at 858da367, GUI surface.

**1. Focus (after merge, an a11y regression).** `SettingsPanel.tsx:264`, the `role="dialog"` root, never takes focus on open and never returns it on close. Opened from the keyboard (gear focused, Enter) focus stays on the gear; Tab lands on the avatar outside the dialog; after Escape focus is wherever it drifted. The repos modal this replaced took focus once on mount and handed it back (DASQEJQ). Only the URL field has `autoFocus`, and only after "link a repo". Reproduced with Playwright reading `document.activeElement`. Also: neither the gear (`aria-pressed`) nor the avatar (`aria-label`) carries `aria-expanded` / `aria-controls` for the dialog.

**2. A rename refetches everything (nit).** `websocket.ts:512-514` broadcasts `repos:changed` unless the answer is `Unchanged`; a label-only change answers `Renamed …`, so every client re-asks the list, the timeline window and the open ticket's commits for a change that moved no commit. The server keeps its clone-log cache for a rename; the clients do not. Reproduced: Enter on the label field sent `repo:add`, `repos:get`, `timeline:get`, `commits:get`.

**Nits.** `SettingsPanel.tsx:161-170` measures `top` on mount and resize only, so a FollowBanner appearing or leaving while the panel is open leaves a gap or an overlap until a resize. Every socket connect sends `repos:get`, and each one spawns `git config --get remote.origin.url` via `readOwnRepo`, even on a board with no repos and the panel never opened. A repo unticked in a wide window and absent from a narrower one has no toggle there and is shown, then hidden again on widening: by design, but it reads as the chart forgetting.

add.issue.name: Other repos: tests that do not bite — the holder's removal-mark path, the signal test without signal-exit, no fetch-on-boot pin; test hygiene

edit.description.md:
Test audit of 4SC2RXY at 858da367: every guard reverted in a pinned worktree and its named test run. 17 of 18 claims went red (URL allowlist, hermetic clone git, 20-repo cap, throttle, lock reclaim, stale-lock age, clone git killed on exit, diff.noprefix pin, squashed-diff dedup, keepPartial, 8MB blob and patch caps, escape stripping, clone flags by location, forged separator, stale git locks, removal mark at fetch start). One stayed green.

**1. The holder's removal-mark path is untested (matters for ZCVKGYT 1).** `commit-repos-fetch-review.test.ts:115` "is deleted by the fetch that held it when it was removed" simulates the holder with a lock file, deletes the lock, then runs a fresh fetch. The fresh fetch honours the mark at its start (`commit-repo-fetch.ts:622`); the `finally` block (:676-679, the holder deleting on the way out) can be removed entirely and the test stays green. ZCVKGYT item 1 (deleteClone throwing before `lock.release()`) lives in exactly that block, so its fix needs a test with a fetch in flight when the mark lands (a slow file:// upstream, or a lock the test releases mid-way).

**2. `clone-git-signal.test.ts` proves the case that is not the bug.** No signal-exit listener beside epiq's handlers, and no SIGHUP case. NZ0SZ72's fix asks for that test.

**3. Nothing asserts "never fetched on boot".** It holds by call structure only: `fetchCommitRepos` is reached from the TUI sync, the GUI's `fetchReposAndBroadcast` and the MCP's `syncThenFetchRepos`; boot never reaches it.

**Untested:** the 32MB clone-log cap and its "too long to read; narrow its window" note; the 120s clone-log timeout and that a timed-out read is not cached (`commit-timeline.ts:193`); the `::` helper guard has no fixture of its own (every `x::` fixture is refused by another rule). Hostile "a checkout that looks like a bare repo" pins git's behaviour, not epiq's: it stays green with `isCloneDir` removed; the location rule is pinned by safe-bare alone.

**Hygiene.** `source/test/setup/global-dir-in-tmp.ts` mkdtemps a global dir per worker and never removes it, so every unit run leaks clone dirs under the OS tmpdir. Two tests sit through the 5s `EXPLICIT_LOCK_WAIT_MS` per run; "past the stats budget" writes and scans a 70MB commit. "keeps a clone whose config could not be read" uses chmod 000 and passes vacuously as root. The lock-contention stress is load-sensitive (acquired > 400 of 900 in 30s).

All after merge, except that item 1 should land with the ZCVKGYT fix.

add.issue.name: Other repos: `:config repoAdd` keeps only the first `=` of an option; the commit hint on Unchanged and Renamed; a broken clone's squash reads as "No commits reference this ticket"

edit.description.md:
Full-feature review of 4SC2RXY at 858da367, TUI and diff-reading surface. All nits, after merge.

1. `repo.cmd.ts:46` — `option.split('=')` keeps the first segment, so `:config repoAdd <url> label=a=b` silently registers `a`; a repeated option (`label=a label=b`) takes the last without a word. Reproduced through `parseRepoAddArgs`.
2. `repo.cmd.ts:88` — the success line appends "commit .epiq/project.json to share it; :sync fetches it" even to `Unchanged` (nothing written) and `Renamed …` (nothing to fetch).
3. `repo.cmd.ts:38` — the TUI's URL refusal says `file://` where every other door says `file:///`.
4. `commit-diff.ts:556` — when a ticket's only matches are in a clone whose squash fails (missing or broken clone), `parts` is empty and the squashed diff says "No commits reference this ticket", contradicting the Code tab's list beside it.

Checked sound on this surface: argv reached only after `repoUrlProblem`, `isRepoLabel`, `isRepoSince` and the enum; remove resolves against the registered list only; no Result thrown; stats batches never straddle repos; patch cap and escape stripping; readme and tool texts match behaviour. MCP binary smoke over scratch repos passed end to end (refusals, add/update/unchanged, dead remote reported not fatal, fork sharing a commit counted once, unpushed commit hidden, remove by label/id/URL, 21st repo refused, project.json byte for byte).
